# Abstract

The complete active Campaign 10 corpus proves no unconditional improvement over the Kominers–Thaler–Zheng exponent 1/3. The strongest coherent route toward 1−o(1) is conditional on one open statement, RDθ: arbitrary labels above the near-linear trigger must either decode directly or yield Ωθ(ε) accepted mass controlled by a common relation of weighted degree Oθ(d). Conditional on RDθ, the remaining characteristic, cleanup, lifting and list-to-one stages are proved below.

# Coverage Receipt

The receipt is frozen at 2026-09-14T11:06:55Z. All 690 non-superseded physical files under `research_state/campaign-10-ultra` were inspected, including every canonical GENIUS/researcher submission, every audit and metadata file, four leaderboards, the 129-entry Lemma Book, all completed roadmap rounds and posts, databases, raw response logs, schemas, stderr files and caches. Across `research_state`, 701 active paths were inventoried. The semantic durable corpus contains 146 files; no active material was omitted. The 37 paths whose directory hierarchy contains `superseded` were outside the active corpus by instruction, and no d≤100 claim was used.

The launch [DATA_MANIFEST.json](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/DATA_MANIFEST.json) declares 15 files and has SHA-256 `343d75e49da76fbab487278e89e8f431ccc37bc29a2da1fafd5d4ba7ef194631`. Eight declared hashes still match. The seven campaign-10 database, job, status and leaderboard files drifted because the campaign continued running. All 11 canonical submission hashes, all nine roadmap round-manifest hashes and all 31 corpus-index receipts recomputed correctly. The boards agree with the audits: two accept, seven revise, one reject, and zero verified benchmark improvements.

# Exponent Ledger

Arora–Sudan's exact bivariate chain is Proposition 18 and Lemma 19 → Lemma 20 → Lemma 21 → Lemma 22, with Theorem 34 and Lemmas 6 and 8, → Theorem 23; Lemma 15 and Theorem 16 yield Corollary 24. The quoted Theorem 23 has `p>C(d+1)^16 ε^−54` and output `cε^45/(d+1)^4`. The normalized trigger and the crude Corollary-24 power 180 are reconstructions, not quoted exponents. See the [author-hosted journal manuscript](https://people.csail.mit.edu/madhu/papers/1997/arora-journ.pdf).

HKSS Theorem 4.3 depends on Claim A.1, Lemma A.2, Claims A.4–A.6, Lemmas A.7–A.8, Claim A.9 and Lemma 2.9. Theorem 4.2 then uses Theorem 4.3, Lemmas 2.1–2.2 and Lemma 3.1; Lemma 3.1 uses Lemma 2.10. Lemmas B.4 and B.6 produce Theorems 4.4 and 1.4. The 1/7 threshold is the algebraic rearrangement of the quoted condition `p>Cd/ε^7`; the printed 1/16 theorem is list-decoding. The displayed v1 proof's sampling range and ε²-versus-ε³ transition remain unresolved in this audit. See [HKSS arXiv v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.12752v1).

KTZ's exact bivariate proof uses preliminary Lemmas 2.1–2.7, then Lemmas 3.1–3.2, 4.1–4.3, 5.1–5.2 and 6.1–6.3. Theorem 1.1 quotes exponent 1/3 and, in dimension two, agreement ε/8000. The bottleneck reconstruction is `|R|=O(p/ε)`, `D=O(sqrt(dp/ε))`, followed by the requirement `D=O(εp)`, hence `ε³=Ω(d/p)`. See [KTZ Revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download) and its [ECCC record](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/).

# Selected Architecture

A-RD is selected. Its high-popularity branch can use researcher-0010, and a localized component can use researcher-0002, but their exponents are not averaged. The remaining low-tail branch is precisely RDθ. Once RDθ supplies D=Oθ(d), the total normalized algebraic and peeling loss is below `(D/p)²+3D/p`, which the near-linear trigger absorbs. Simple-root KTZ lifting gives one polynomial per component. Because every component polynomial satisfies `B(X,Y,Q)=0`, each `Z−Q` divides B; at most `deg_Z(B)≤D/d≤Kθ` distinct templates occur. Pigeonholing therefore returns one polynomial rather than merely a list.

# Limitations

This is an honest conditional theorem, not an unconditional benchmark improvement. RDθ remains unproved, the integrated reduction is newly synthesized rather than verifier-accepted, and exact exponent one is false. The statement is only for prime fields, dimension two and integer 100<d<p. Near d=p it may be vacuous through its constants, and no computational experiment is used as proof.

proof_steps.proof: The exact external package is KTZ Revision 1, Lemmas 2.5–2.7 and 6.1–6.3: a nonzero base polynomial of degree at most D cannot vanish formally on more than D affine lines; two coprime polynomials of total degrees u,v share at most uv polynomial graph lines; a simple root has a unique formal Newton lift; more than D incident graph lines turn that lift into a total-degree-d polynomial identity; and simple-root uniqueness propagates it through a connected accepted component. Restriction of weighted degree D to a degree-d graph has univariate degree at most D.
proof_steps.statement: Record the exact primary-source algebraic facts used downstream.

proof_steps.proof: This is the sole assumed mathematical statement. Its formal rank condition means a nonzero kernel, not failure of surjectivity; its reaching points are distinct and use another selected line.
proof_steps.statement: Assume RDθ with constants Cθ,Kθ,aθ,cθ and Cθ≥8Kθ/aθ.

proof_steps.proof: Put ρ=d/p and x=D/p. From ε≥Cθρ^(1−θ) and D≤Kθd, x≤(Kθ/Cθ)ερ^θ≤aθ ε/8≤1/8. Hence D<p. Moreover x²+3x≤25x/8≤25aθ ε/64<aθ ε/2.
proof_steps.statement: The structured branch is characteristic-safe and has enough deletion budget.

proof_steps.proof: Rank deficiency gives nonzero A₀∈ker Φ_{R,D}. Replace it by its squarefree radical A. Every selected graph identity survives because F_p[t] is a domain, and weighted degree does not increase. If A were Z-independent, the linear equation of each of the more than D selected lines would divide a nonzero base polynomial of degree at most D, impossible. Thus A is Z-dependent; D
proof_steps.statement: Extract a squarefree Z-dependent relation A of weighted degree at most D on every selected graph.

proof_steps.proof: Let x be a reaching point on L and on M∈R\{L}. Acceptedness gives P_L(x)=f(x)=P_M(x), while the selected identity gives A(x,P_M(x))=0. Thus A(ell_L(t),P_L(t)) has more than D distinct roots and degree at most D, so it is identically zero.
proof_steps.statement: Extend the formal identity from R to every line in T.

proof_steps.proof: Write A=HB, where H∈F_p[X,Y] is the gcd of the Z-coefficients and B is primitive. Since A is squarefree, B is squarefree and Z-dependent. On a line where H does not vanish identically, cancellation in the domain F_p[t] gives B(ell_L(t),P_L(t))≡0. At most deg(H)≤D lines are content lines.
proof_steps.statement: Remove content and obtain a primitive squarefree relation B on all other target graphs.

proof_steps.proof: If an irreducible factor C divided both B and B_Z, squarefreeness would force C_Z=0. Because deg_Z(C)<p, C would be Z-independent, contradicting primitivity. Hence gcd(B,B_Z)=1.
proof_steps.statement: The primitive relation is vertically separable in every legal structured branch.

proof_steps.proof: KTZ Lemma 2.6 applied to B and B_Z bounds graph lines on which both vanish formally by D(D−1). Together with at most D content lines, their normalized mass is at most D²/[p(p+1)]≤(D/p)². On every other line, B_Z(ell_L,P_L) is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most D−d, so its zero incidences have normalized mass at most (D−d)/p≤D/p. Every retained incidence satisfies B(x,f(x))=0 and B_Z(x,f(x))≠0.
proof_steps.statement: Direct vertical cleanup costs at most (D/p)²+D/p.

proof_steps.proof: Repeatedly remove each current point or line vertex of degree at most D. Charge every removed edge when its first endpoint is deleted. Point deletions cost below D/(p+1), line deletions at most D/p, hence less than 2D/p in total. By P2 and P7, total deletion is below (D/p)²+3D/p<aθ ε/2. A nonempty G₁ remains with edge mass at least aθ ε/2 and minimum degree greater than D.
proof_steps.statement: Produce a clean high-minimum-degree graph retaining at least half the certificate mass.

proof_steps.proof: In any connected component Γ choose a point b. More than D distinct incident lines meet the simple root (b,f(b)), so KTZ Lemma 6.1 supplies a total-degree-d QΓ with B(X,Y,QΓ)=0 and QΓ restricted to each incident line equal to its label. KTZ Lemma 6.3 propagates this equality along every edge using simple-root uniqueness. Thus QΓ=f at every point vertex of Γ.
proof_steps.statement: Every connected component supplies one valid degree-d polynomial template.

proof_steps.proof: Evaluation at Z=QΓ has kernel generated by Z−QΓ, so B(X,Y,QΓ)=0 implies Z−QΓ divides B. Distinct QΓ give distinct monic irreducible factors. Therefore at most deg_Z(B)≤wdeg(B)/d≤D/d≤Kθ distinct templates occur.
proof_steps.statement: Compress all component polynomials to a list of size at most Kθ.
